relations.note: Poseidon is Polyphemus’s father by the sea-nymph Thoosa.

relations.myth: Polyphemus invokes Poseidon’s curse against Odysseus
relations.note: Poseidon hears his prayer and obstructs Odysseus’s return.
Thoosa is Polyphemus’s mother by Poseidon.
Phorcys is Polyphemus’s maternal grandfather through Thoosa.

relations.myth: Polyphemus rejects Zeus’s protection of strangers
relations.note: He contemptuously declares that Cyclopes care nothing for Zeus.
Odysseus intoxicates Polyphemus using wine associated with Dionysus.
Polyphemus courts Galatea through music, but their relationship remains uncertain.

relations.myth: The lovesick shepherd sings to Galatea
relations.note: He offers Galatea pastoral gifts and cave life but remains unsuccessful.

relations.myth: Galatea teasingly pursues an indifferent Polyphemus
relations.note: Galatea throws apples and provokes him while he feigns indifference.

relations.myth: Polyphemus and Galatea appear as affectionate lovers
relations.note: Campanian paintings depict mutual affection, correspondence, or erotic union.
Appian makes Galatea Polyphemus’s mate and mother of their sons.

relations.myth: Polyphemus establishes Galatea’s shrine near Etna
relations.note: Duris reportedly credited him with founding her shrine amid pastoral abundance.

relations.myth: Polyphemus crushes Acis with a rock
relations.note: Jealous of Galatea’s lover, Polyphemus kills Acis, who becomes a river-god.
Appian names Celtus as a son of Polyphemus and Galatea.
Appian names Illyrius as a son of Polyphemus and Galatea.
Appian names Galas as a son of Polyphemus and Galatea.

relations.myth: The cave, blinding, escape, and curse
relations.note: Polyphemus eats Odysseus’s men before Odysseus blinds and escapes him.

relations.myth: Odysseus uses wine and the Nobody name-trick
relations.note: Odysseus intoxicates him, gives the name Nobody, and escapes beneath rams.

relations.myth: Telemus foretells Polyphemus’s blinding by Odysseus
relations.note: Polyphemus recalls Telemus’s prophecy after Odysseus reveals his identity.
Silenus serves Polyphemus as a slave until Odysseus defeats him.
The satyrs serve him unwillingly and join Odysseus after his blinding.
They mistake the Nobody wordplay and advise him to pray to Poseidon.

relations.myth: Eros carries Galatea’s message to Polyphemus
relations.note: A winged Eros delivers Galatea’s message in Pompeian imagery.

relations.myth: Aeneas escapes the blinded Cyclops coast
relations.note: Aeneas’s Trojans encounter the wounded Polyphemus and flee his gathering kin.
The abandoned Greek warns Aeneas before Polyphemus appears with his flock.
